Como hemos observado en los ejemplos precedentes en japreria, el acento de intensidad recae sobre la última sílaba. El cambio de acento hacia la primera sílaba se presenta en aquellas palabras cuya composición silábica es más compleja, palabras de tres o cuatro sílabas, el acento de intensidad ocurre en la primera sílaba.

new_statements.translation: The intensity accent in Yukpa falls on the penultimate syllable, although it is very weak [and] can shift to any syllable. As we have observed in the preceding examples, in Japreria the intensity accent falls on the last syllable. The shift of the accent to the first syllable appears in those words whose syllabic composition is more complex; [in] words of three or four syllables the intensity accent occurs on the first syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Per Oquendo (impressionistic, no acoustic data): Japreria word stress is final in (the predominantly disyllabic) words, but in longer words of three or four syllables stress falls on the first syllable. His 2020 follow-up (Boletín Antropológico 99, p.58, pp.69-70; file) repeats the initial-stress-in-3-4-syllable-words claim (kamuneshi, kuvenesi, kepa, krenka), calls Japreria stress 'asimétrico' and dependent on 'ciertas condiciones y restricciones' (unlike Yukpa's heavy-syllable-else-initial pattern), and for CV.CV words says stress is on the 2nd syllable when that syllable begins with a fricative (mashe 'largo', kase 'cesta'); the exposition breaks off after that. Net: length-dependent edge (final in short words, initial in long words) with a segmental condition -- not a single fixed position, hence coded unclear-or-contradictory rather than fixed-final or fixed-initial.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in either article.
new_statements.exceptions: Three- and four-syllable words take initial stress (2004, 2020). 2020 adds: in CV.CV words the second syllable is stressed when it begins with a fricative (implying other disyllables may differ; not spelled out).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level 'acento de intensidad' on isolated lexical items (elicited wordlist/citation forms); contrasted throughout with Yukpa (penult per Oquendo 2004; heavy-syllable-else-initial / penult per Oquendo, Morales y Maestros yukpa 2007 as quoted in Oquendo 2020). No phrase-level discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: Both Oquendo articles describe Japrería (japr1238, jru) of the single Japreria community in the Sierra de Perijá, Zulia, explicitly as a language distinct from Yukpa (yukp1241; his Yukpa data are Irapa/Tokuko varieties). The Yukpa stress remarks in the same passages belong to yukp1241, not to Japrería.

sources.note: p.72 (Conclusiones): Yukpa intensity accent on the penult (weak, mobile); in Japreria the intensity accent falls on the LAST syllable; in words of more complex syllabic make-up (three or four syllables) the accent shifts to the FIRST syllable. Examples in the body are not systematically stress-marked (only [píšRa] 'pájaro' carries an acute).
